brief: Cats
note: Sparse baseline on a small tag (Cats, 17 records); tests whether a cat in the corner of a genre scene counts.

brief: Ruins
note: Sparse; capriccios, Roman views and ruined stables in Nativities all compete.

brief: Self-portraits
note: Over-popular category; a fact about the work, not visible in the image, so it rests on title and tags.

brief: Waterfalls
note: Sparse, concrete subject; is a small cascade in the background enough?

brief: Sadness
note: Abstract emotion in one word: Lamentations, mourning portraits and melancholy landscapes are all plausible readings. Where taste varies most.

brief: Bridges
note: Many bridges sit untagged inside landscapes; needs the image.

brief: Lions
note: Ambiguous: animal studies, Daniel, Saint Jerome's lion, heraldic lions. Does a lion as a saint's attribute count?

brief: Evening light
note: Aesthetic, not a subject; the Evening tag is small and the quality of light is mostly visible only in the image.

brief: Musicians playing lutes or guitars in candlelit taverns, for a live-music venue's posters
note: Two conditions (instrument, setting) plus lighting; a lute player in a portrait fits the instrument but not the tavern.

brief: Bedrooms with rumpled linen, intimate but not erotic, for a bedding brand's lookbook
note: Boundary case: many bed scenes are nudes or deathbeds. Tests the exclusion and whether religious births in bedrooms fit.

brief: Tall ships at anchor in a calm harbour, for a maritime museum shop
note: Opposite of d20/d34 (storms): calm water is the condition.

brief: Allegories of the senses or the seasons, for a school slideshow
note: Iconographic: a figure smelling a flower may be 'Smell' or just a portrait. Rests on titles.

brief: Skulls and memento mori, quiet rather than gruesome, for a philosophy podcast cover
note: Vanitas still lifes and Saint Jerome or Magdalene with a skull; 'quiet' rules out martyrdoms.

brief: Peasants resting after the harvest, for a bakery's packaging
note: Activity plus moment: harvest scenes with people working fit partly; resting is the qualifier.

brief: Cavalry battle scenes full of movement, for a history documentary's title sequence
note: Overlaps Horses (117) and Battles (11); single equestrian portraits should not fit.

brief: Portraits in which a Black sitter is the subject, not a servant or attendant, for a school unit on representation in European art
note: Culturally sensitive and likely thin in the corpus; tests the exclusion of subordinate figures and whether the system returns few results rather than off-brief ones.

brief: Something that feels like a rainy Sunday afternoon, for a cafe's playlist artwork
note: Pure mood: quiet interiors, grey weather and idle figures are all readings. Few records show rain.

brief: A single figure seen from behind at a window or doorway, looking out at the light; quiet and contemplative, soft daylight, uncluttered; for a meditation app's onboarding screens
note: Compositional (figure from behind) and rarely tagged; relies on the image. Grade 1 for a window scene with the figure facing us.

brief: Lavish banquet or dining scenes with silver, glass and abundant food, candlelight, rich reds and golds, for a wine merchant's Christmas catalogue
note: Banquet still lifes without people and feasts with people both fit; palette and candlelight decide the grade.

brief: Eighteenth-century French gardens or parks with fountains and strolling couples, pastel palette, lighthearted, for a patisserie rebrand
note: Period, nationality, subject and mood together; a fete galante without a fountain fits partly.

brief: Beaches with fishermen hauling nets or boats, overcast northern light, grey-blue palette, no pleasure boats or bathers, for a sustainable seafood label
note: Two exclusions plus a palette; tests whether leisure beach scenes are kept out.

brief: A scholar or saint in a study with books and a skull, dim interior light, absorbed in reading or writing, for a university library's exhibition banner
note: Saint Jerome is the obvious answer; tests whether secular scholars and philosophers are found too.

brief: Animal paintings where the animal has personality: a dog, cat or horse looking straight out at the viewer, warm palette, plain background, for a veterinary clinic's waiting-room prints
note: Gaze and character are visible only in the image; overlaps d40 (dogs in domestic portraits) but the animal must be the subject.

brief: Nineteenth-century Paris streets with wet pavements, umbrellas and carriages, grey light, for a fashion brand's autumn film moodboard
note: Over-popular reference (the best-known rainy Paris street painting is not in the Met corpus); tests partial fits rather than the famous one.

brief: A single face lit out of deep black, strong chiaroscuro, theatrical, any subject or period, for a theatre company's season brochure
note: Aesthetic over subject; differs from d31 (still life) and d39 (young men) by allowing any subject. Tests image-led retrieval.
